answer: Coordination Tariff Ledger. Each agent action that references another identity’s output pays a small ledger fee proportional to the referenced cluster’s recent distinct-actor count. The dune of past references is recomputed per epoch, so a sybil ring must pay repeated fees to simulate independent corroboration. Fees route to unrelated agents via a rotating whisper channel, not the referrer. An attacker’s per-identity cost is the summed tariff for every fabricated link; a lantern audit checks fee path diversity and voids unmatched clusters.
